proposals.after: He rose to vice censor-in-chief on the Jiangnan Branch Censorate and was appointed Hanlin expositor-in-chief, drafter of proclamations, concurrent national history compiler, and director of the classics mat.

proposals.before: Flooding on the Hutuo River was harming Zhending. Qiyan argued that ennobling the river god as a marquis was misguided, sent an official rebuke, repaired the dikes, and dredged the choked channels until the floods subsided.
proposals.after: Flooding on the Hutuo River was harming Zhending. Qiyan proposed ennobling the river god as a marquis, sent an official rebuke, repaired the dikes, and dredged the choked channels until the floods subsided.
proposals.reason: 論封河神為侯爵 states that he discussed or proposed conferring a marquisate, not that he condemned the enfeoffment as misguided.

proposals.before: The waters of the Hutuo River harmed Zhending; Qiyan argued that enfeoffing the river god as marquis was wrong, and sent an official communication to reprove it; he again repaired the dikes, dredged the choked and stagnant channels, and the flood harm then ceased.
proposals.after: The waters of the Hutuo River harmed Zhending; Qiyan argued for enfeoffing the river god as marquis, and sent an official communication to reprove it; he again repaired the dikes, dredged the choked and stagnant channels, and the flood harm then ceased.
proposals.reason: 論封 does not mean he judged the enfeoffment wrong; the English adds was wrong, reversing the likely sense.

proposals.before: His great-great-grandfather Xin was the first to move the family to Liuyang, so Xuan was counted as a native of Liuyang.
proposals.after: His great-grandfather Xin was the first to move the family to Liuyang, so Xuan was counted as a native of Liuyang.

proposals.before: By his great-great-grandfather Xin they first moved to settle at Liuyang; therefore Xuan was a man of Liuyang.
proposals.after: By his great-grandfather Xin they first moved to settle at Liuyang; therefore Xuan was a man of Liuyang.
proposals.reason: 曾大父 corresponds to great-grandfather, not great-great-grandfather.

proposals.before: In the fifth year of the renewed Zhizhi era his legs were afflicted with paralysis. He asked to return south for medical care, but the emperor refused.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of the renewed Zhiyuan era his legs were afflicted with paralysis. He asked to return south for medical care, but the emperor refused.
proposals.reason: 重紀至元 is the restored Zhiyuan era, not Zhizhi (至治).

proposals.before: In the fifth year of the renewed Zhizhi era his feet suffered wind paralysis; he begged to return south for convenient medical treatment, and the emperor did not approve.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of the renewed Zhiyuan era his feet suffered wind paralysis; he begged to return south for convenient medical treatment, and the emperor did not approve.
proposals.reason: The Chinese era is 至元, not 至治/Zhizhi.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yanyou, when the civil service examination was restored, Xuan submitted his writings for recommendation.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yanyou, when the civil service examination was restored, Xuan entered as a recommended candidate in the Book of Documents.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yanyou an edict established the examination to select scholars; Xuan presented himself for recommendation with his writings.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yanyou an edict established the examination to select scholars; Xuan was presented for recommendation in the Book of Documents.

proposals.after: The central secretariat reported his death. proposals.before: The Central Secretariat reported it; the emperor bestowed funeral gifts in very generous measure, granted the title Meritorious Minister of Honoring Benevolence, Illuminating Virtue, Promoting Loyalty, and Upholding Rectitude, Grand Preceptor, and Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu, and gave the posthumous title Wen.

proposals.before: Over more than forty years in office, the days he spent at court amounted to roughly four parts out of five.
proposals.after: Over more than forty years in office, the days he spent at court amounted to roughly three parts out of four.
proposals.reason: Chinese 四之三 means three quarters (three of four), not four fifths; the idiomatic already has three quarters.

proposals.before: Xuan had no son; he took his nephew Daolao as heir, but Daolao again died before Xuan.
proposals.after: Xuan had no son; he took his nephew Daolao as heir, but Daolao then died before Xuan.
proposals.reason: Here 复 marks sequence/contrast (then/but), not a second prior death; 'again died' invents an extra death.

proposals.before: Qarachu darughachi Wanbu, relying on the chancellor's backing, served in the Eastern Palace guard. His conduct was grossly licentious. When censors impeached him, he hid in the censor-in-chief's house. Youren seized him and had him removed.
proposals.after: Wanbu, darughachi of Huifu, relying on the chancellor's backing, served in the Eastern Palace guard. His conduct was grossly licentious. When censors impeached him, he hid in the censor-in-chief's house. Youren seized him and had him removed.
proposals.reason: 會福達魯花赤 is the darughachi of Huifu (會福), not the ethnonym Qarachu.

proposals.before: The court proposed reviving ancient mutilation punishments, establishing a mobile pacification commission, and forbidding Han Chinese and Southerners to study Mongol and Uyghur script. Youren fought each proposal and blocked them.
proposals.after: The court proposed reviving ancient mutilation punishments, establishing a branch Bureau of Military Affairs, and forbidding Han Chinese and Southerners to study Mongol and Uyghur script. Youren fought each proposal and blocked them.
proposals.reason: 行樞密院 is a mobile/branch privy council (military affairs), not a pacification commission.

proposals.before: At the start of the renewed Zhizhi era, Han Gongpu of Changlu triggered a major case over weapons found in his home. proposals.after: At the start of the renewed Zhiyuan era, Han Gongpu of Changlu triggered a major case over weapons found in his home. It swept through the censorate and secretariat, and many officials fell on corruption charges, but Youren's name was never implicated, which only sharpened the resentment against him.
proposals.reason: 重紀至元 is the renewed Zhiyuan era, not Zhizhi.

proposals.before: At the beginning of the renewed Zhizhi era, Han Gongpu of Changlu, because of weapons hidden in his household, triggered a great case that implicated the censorate and secretariat; many were ruined for corruption, but Youren's name alone was not among them, and so those who resented him grew even fiercer.
proposals.after: At the beginning of the renewed Zhiyuan era, Han Gongpu of Changlu, because of weapons hidden in his household, triggered a great case that implicated the censorate and secretariat; many were ruined for corruption, but Youren's name alone was not among them, and so those who resented him grew even fiercer.
